# Examples

Each example is a self-contained folder: a jupytext "percent" Python script, a
README, and a gitignored `output/` for figures.

| Example | Title | What it shows |
|---------|-------|---------------|
| [aldp_potential_jaxmm](aldp_potential_jaxmm/) | Alanine Dipeptide Potential Energy with jaxmm | Evaluate the potential energy of alanine dipeptide (22 atoms, 66 DOF) using jaxmm, |
| [custom_energy](custom_energy/) | Custom Energy Terms and Restraints (needs py3Dmol) | jaxmm energy functions are composable: you can combine total_energy with |
| [custom_samplers](custom_samplers/) | Building Custom Samplers with baoab_step | jaxmm exposes baoab_step as a building block for constructing custom |
| [differentiable_md](differentiable_md/) | Differentiable Molecular Dynamics | Because jaxmm is pure JAX, we can differentiate *through* entire MD trajectories. |
| [energy_landscape](energy_landscape/) | Potential Energy Landscape of Alanine Dipeptide (needs py3Dmol) | Visualize the free energy surface F(phi, psi) of alanine dipeptide by sampling |
| [free_energy](free_energy/) | Free Energy Estimation | Estimate the free energy surface of alanine dipeptide from MD sampling. |
| [jaxmm_demo](jaxmm_demo/) | jaxmm Demo: Pure JAX Molecular Potential Energy (needs py3Dmol) | This example demonstrates jaxmm, a pure JAX replacement for OpenMM's energy evaluation. |
| [normal_modes](normal_modes/) | Normal Mode Analysis with jax.hessian (needs py3Dmol) | Compute vibrational normal modes of alanine dipeptide at a potential energy |
| [parallel_tempering](parallel_tempering/) | Parallel Tempering MD for Accurate Ramachandran Plots | Single-temperature Langevin at 300K gets trapped in local basins of the Ramachandran plot |
| [quickstart](quickstart/) | jaxmm Quick Start (needs py3Dmol) | Core API in 5 minutes. Extract force field parameters from OpenMM once, |
| [solvent_comparison](solvent_comparison/) | Vacuum vs Implicit Solvent (needs py3Dmol) | Side-by-side comparison of alanine dipeptide in vacuum and implicit solvent |

## Running

```bash
pip install -e ".[examples]"                     # matplotlib, py3Dmol, jupytext
python examples/quickstart/quickstart.py         # run one
python tools/render_examples.py                  # run all, save figures
python tools/render_examples.py --only quickstart
```

Figures land in each example's `output/`, which is gitignored. Most examples
finish in well under a minute. `parallel_tempering` is the slowest at about 11
minutes, because it runs 10 replicas, and `free_energy` does 500k MD steps. The
renderer's default 900s per-example timeout covers both; only lower it if you
know what you are skipping.

These are plain Python, not notebooks. `# %%` marks a cell, so Jupyter and VS
Code open them as notebooks when jupytext is installed, and they also run as
ordinary scripts. Notebooks are deliberately not committed: stored outputs are
base64 blobs that bloat the repository and produce diffs nobody can review.
